content:
morgan: Heads up — seeing a surge of GPU nodes in us-west2a entering NotReady with NoSchedule ~10:15 UTC. Device plugin process appears to start then drop registration. :thinking_face:
lee: I see it too, we got an autoscaler spike then a series of node flaps. Any recent kernel or image push to that pool?
sasha: No kernel push this morning. We did a Calico policy update last night for MTU enforcement. Could be related.
devon: infra-bot just posted these alerts:
k8s-bot: [ALERT] gpu-nodepool-us-west2a: 6 nodes NotReady (device-plugin failed to register)
infra-bot: autoscaler: scaled up +8 (requests pending), then scaled down -5 within 3m due to low cpu.
morgan: Paste of kubelet/device-plugin snippets:```
I0310 10:14:32.123 kubelet.go:344] Starting device plugin watcher
E0310 10:14:35.456 device_plugin.go:78] grpc: received transport-level error: connection closed
E0310 10:14:35.457 kubelet.go:512] Failed to register plugin: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed
```
lee: That looks like intermittent network close between kubelet and plugin socket. Any MTU/encapsulation changes?
sasha: Calico MTU changed from 1500 -> 1420 in the policy to account for GCP overlay. Could be fragmentation causing gRPC timeouts for unix sockets?
devon: Also noticed a bunch of conntrack entries on the nodes: `nf_conntrack_count` near limit. kube-proxy logs show conntrack dropped some NAT flows. Might be related to load from health probes during scale events.
oncall: quick checks: can someone run `ss -xap | grep device-plugin` on a flaky node and `sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max`?
morgan: Ran checks on node gpu-uw2a-03:```
# ss -xap | grep nvidia
unix  2      [ ACC ]     STREAM     LISTENING     12345    2050/kubelet 
unix  2      [ ]         DGRAM                    23456    7890/nvidia-device-plugin
# cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
262144
# cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
260980
```
sasha: conntrack_count pretty high, but below max. However kube-proxy had logs about ENOMEM earlier. Could be OOMKill on device plugin container then rapid restarts causing socket piles.
lee: Any cgroup or oom logs?
morgan: `dmesg` shows oom_killer invoked around the time of plugin restarts on two nodes: "Out of memory: Kill process 7890 (nvidia-device-*)"
devon: Which image are device plugin pods running? If they pulled a new plugin image with higher mem, combined with bursty autoscaler startup we could exhaust memory footprint.
sasha: It's the pinned image `nvidia/dp:2.4.0` (unchanged). But the kernel module update last week included `nvidia-520` driver, which increased GPU driver daemon memory footprint.
oncall: So stack: autoscaler spins up nodes to meet pending GPU pods -> Calico MTU change + heavy probe traffic + kube-proxy conntrack close to limit + driver/plugin memory bump -> plugin restarts/GRPC closes -> kubelet marks node NotReady/NoSchedule. Also autoscaler reacting and removing nodes prematurely -> churn.
lee: Sounds plausible. Short-term mitigation options?
sasha: 1) Pin autoscaler max surge and increase scale-down delay to avoid immediate scale-in.
2) Increase nf_conntrack_max and monitor (safely, via sysctl on pool template).
3) Add oom_score_adj / memory limits to device-plugin daemonset to prevent host OOM kills.
4) Rollback Calico MTU change to 1500 for the GPU pool as an experiment.
devon: Also add a readiness probe to device-plugin so kubelet doesn't mark node NotReady instantly; allow a graceful registration window.
morgan: I can flip scale-down delay for that nodepool to 15m and bump conntrack to 300k via a config change. Will also add limits to daemonset tomorrow morning.
lee: For immediate triage, can we cordon the most flaky nodes and drain non-critical GPU pods to prevent further OOMs?
sasha: I'll cordon gpu-uw2a-02 and gpu-uw2a-07. Please avoid draining long-running training jobs until backup capacity is ready.
oncall: Reminder: keep Cost team in the loop — increasing conntrack or scale-up delays may increase bill. We'll note tradeoffs.
infra-bot: ACTION: morgan to apply autoscaler config change. sasha to cordon two nodes. devon to prepare device-plugin limits PR.
morgan: Applied scale-down-delay=900s and max-unneeded=2 for pool GPU-us-west2a. Monitoring now.
lee: After scale-delay change we still saw 1 node go NotReady but no immediate scale-in after that. Health seems more stable.
sasha: I'll revert Calico MTU on a canary node tomorrow and watch gRPC restarts. If that fixes registration, we'll schedule a rollout plan.
devon: Will draft PR for device-plugin resource requests/limits and readiness probe. Suggest request: 150Mi, limit: 400Mi, readiness probe: exec `stat /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/nvidia.sock` (or similar) with initialDelay 10s and period 5s.
morgan: Good. Also enabling extra logging on kube-proxy for conntrack evictions.
lee: Thanks team. Keep this thread updated. If things worsen, escalate to infra pager. :loudspeaker:
